scope: Public information from Oops I AI’d Again. No private conversations, client records or inbox content.

sources.title: About Thom
facts: Thom Hamilton is a business owner, filmmaker, maker and founder of Next to Kin, based in Regina, Saskatchewan.
He calls his role AI Alchemist. He did not set out to become an AI expert and does not claim to be one.
He directs, connects, reviews and refines work with multiple AI tools. He makes decisions, checks results, does physical making and fixes mistakes.

sources.title: Actual work
facts: Public examples include physical programmed NFC KinTags, AI-assisted artwork reviewed for production, prepared outreach letters and a working process atlas.
The displayed outreach letter is prepared work, not proof of a send, partnership or endorsement.
Some work is built or used; some is acceptance-tested, paused or a prototype. These labels do not guarantee current reliability.

sources.title: Whitetail Films example
facts: Thom also runs Whitetail Films. He rebuilt around the functions he actually used after subscriptions gained unneeded functions and prices grew faster than bookings.

The connected build brings together the public website, project dashboard, contracts, planning portal and photo/film delivery. It covers roles previously served by Squarespace, HoneyBook, Pic-Time and Vidflow.
Thom set requirements and reviewed the result. Claude Code implemented it with a Codex security review.
Payment tracking is separate from payment processing. Adoption varies; no verified savings figure or complete migration is claimed.
Screenshots include a saved dashboard, a real portal rendered with labelled sample data, and a delivery-verification collection.

sources.title: Start with a problem
facts: The approach starts with a recurring frustration rather than choosing an AI tool first: repeated typing, missed follow-ups, scattered files, repeated paperwork or waiting on handoffs.
Useful first steps gather checked information once, carry it into the next step, and keep human decisions where judgment matters.

AI implementation starts at $999 CAD for a clearly defined problem. Scope, inclusions and price are agreed before work starts. Larger builds are quoted separately. Any ongoing software, hosting or support costs are explained separately. This is a starting price, not a promise that every project costs $999. No hourly rate, standard delivery deadline or guarantee is published.

sources.title: Try a tool
facts: The website check reads up to four public HTML pages and gives ten qualitative findings with practical next steps. It is an AI-generated first pass, not a performance grade, sales prediction or complete audit.
It does not test page speed, accessibility, search rankings, video playback or form delivery. Text can be pasted if automated reading fails.

The fresh-angle tool at /#talk takes a recurring business headache and offers an AI-generated angle and a small experiment. Its answer appears on the page. Nothing is emailed to Thom unless the visitor chooses to send it.

sources.title: Book a call
facts: Visitors can book a 30-minute Google Meet with Thom through his Google booking page. Meeting details are added after booking.
The assistant cannot see live availability, book a time, send an email, promise a price or make commitments on Thom’s behalf. The visitor completes booking on Google.
Public email contact is support@nexttokin.ca.

sources.title: AI implementation pricing
facts: AI implementation starting at $999 CAD. Scope and price agreed before work begins; larger builds quoted separately. Ongoing software, hosting or support costs explained separately.

sources.title: Conference and sales outreach example
facts: Thom used a research-led preparation and outreach process for his own Next to Kin / KinTag campaign at ACCA 2026 in Calgary, October 7–9.

The supplied campaign summary reports 168 event listings merged into 121 organisations, 20 letter variants for the top 10, a 12-page meeting briefing, and 11 personal replies, separately from auto-replies and bounces. These are self-reported campaign records, not independently audited sales results.

Prepared materials include ranked prospects, sourced public people research, verified identification photos where available, personal email drafts, print-ready letters, reply notes, booth briefings and follow-up drafts.
The client checks research, chooses targets, approves and sends messages, and has conversations. No automatic outreach or guaranteed attendance, meetings, leads, revenue or conversion is promised.

The process can be adapted to conferences, trade shows, account research and sales-team follow-up. Full event campaigns are scoped and quoted separately; $999 CAD is a general AI implementation starting price, not a whole conference package price.
